destinations.name: Abu Dhabi
destinations.season_note: Winter sun season; summers are extremely hot.

highlights.title: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
highlights.snippet: The crown jewel of Abu Dhabi and one of the world's largest mosques. The white marble facade, 82 domes, and 1,000 columns are staggering.

highlights.title: Louvre Abu Dhabi, Saadiyat Island
highlights.snippet: Jean Nouvel's masterpiece — a "rain of light" dome sheltering galleries that trace human civilization from ancient Mesopotamia to contemporary art.

highlights.title: Yas Island Theme Parks
highlights.snippet: Abu Dhabi's entertainment mega-complex includes **Ferrari World** (home to Formula Rossa, the world's fastest roller coaster at 240 km/h — tickets AED 395/$108), **Warner Bros.

highlights.title: Desert Safari with Dune Bashing
highlights.snippet: The quintessential Gulf experience. A 4x4 picks you up from your hotel for an afternoon of dune bashing in the Al Khatim desert, followed by a traditional Bedouin camp dinner with shisha, henna pai…

highlights.title: The Corniche & Heritage Village
highlights.snippet: Abu Dhabi's waterfront promenade stretches 8 km along the coast with manicured gardens, cycling paths, and public beaches.

destinations.name: Alaska
destinations.season_note: Midnight-sun summer; cruise season. Aurora viewing is Sep–Mar.

highlights.title: Glacier Bay National Park
highlights.snippet: Accessible primarily by cruise ship or small charter boat, Glacier Bay is the crown jewel of Alaska tourism. Watch massive tidewater glaciers calve icebergs into the sea from the deck of your ship.

highlights.title: Denali National Park
highlights.snippet: Home to Denali (Mount McKinley), the tallest peak in North America at 20,310 feet. The park road extends 92 miles into wilderness, but private vehicles can only drive the first 15 miles.

highlights.title: Kenai Fjords National Park, Seward
highlights.snippet: Take the Major Marine Tours 6-hour cruise ($200/adult, $130/child) from Seward to see humpback whales, orcas, sea otters, puffins, and the Exit Glacier. The wildlife is almost guaranteed in summer.

highlights.title: Mendenhall Glacier, Juneau
highlights.snippet: One of the most accessible glaciers in Alaska, just 12 miles from downtown Juneau. Hike the moderate Trail of Time (2.4 miles round trip) to the glacier viewing area.

highlights.title: Inside Passage Cruise
highlights.snippet: A 7-day cruise through Alaska's Inside Passage — typically Seattle/Vancouver to Juneau, Skagway, Ketchikan, and Glacier Bay — is the most popular way to see Alaska.

destinations.name: Aruba
destinations.season_note: Outside the hurricane belt — reliably dry and breezy most of the year.

highlights.title: Eagle Beach
highlights.snippet: Consistently voted one of the top ten beaches in the world, and it earns it. The sand is powder-white, the water is calm and impossibly blue, and the beach is wide enough that it never feels crowde…

highlights.title: Arikok National Park
highlights.snippet: This rugged desert landscape covering nearly 20% of the island is Aruba's wild side.

highlights.title: Snorkeling at Arashi Beach & Antilla Shipwreck
highlights.snippet: Arashi Beach, at the island's northern tip, has excellent shore snorkeling with sea turtles and tropical fish in shallow, calm water.

highlights.title: California Lighthouse & Alto Vista Chapel
highlights.snippet: The California Lighthouse at the island's northwest tip offers sweeping views and gorgeous sunsets.

highlights.title: Downtown Oranjestad
highlights.snippet: The capital city is a charming mix of pastel-colored Dutch colonial buildings, duty-free shopping, and waterfront restaurants.

destinations.name: Australia
destinations.season_note: Southern-hemisphere spring/autumn are the sweet spots for Sydney & Melbourne.

highlights.title: Great Barrier Reef, Queensland
highlights.snippet: The largest living structure on earth stretches over 2,300 km. Snorkel or dive from Cairns or the Whitsunday Islands. Take a scenic helicopter flight for the aerial perspective.

highlights.title: Sydney Harbour: Opera House & Bridge
highlights.snippet: Walk across the Harbour Bridge or climb it (BridgeClimb, $200–350 AUD). Take a ferry to Manly Beach. Watch a performance at the Opera House — the building is more impressive inside than out.

highlights.title: Great Ocean Road, Victoria
highlights.snippet: One of the world's greatest coastal drives. The Twelve Apostles limestone stacks, Loch Ard Gorge, and the surf town of Torquay are the highlights.

highlights.title: Uluru (Ayers Rock), Northern Territory
highlights.snippet: The sacred red monolith at sunrise or sunset is a spiritual experience. Climbing is now prohibited (and was always culturally inappropriate).

highlights.title: Melbourne: Coffee, Laneways & Cricket
highlights.snippet: Melbourne is Australia's culture and food capital. Explore the street-art-covered laneways, drink flat whites in hidden cafés, and watch cricket at the MCG — the cathedral of the sport.

destinations.name: Bahamas
destinations.season_note: Dry season; hurricane risk peaks Aug–Oct.

highlights.title: Atlantis Aquaventure Water Park, Paradise Island
highlights.snippet: The centerpiece of any Bahamas family trip. Over 20 million gallons of water, the Leap of Faith slide that drops you through a shark-filled lagoon, and a mile-long lazy river system.

highlights.title: Swimming Pigs at Big Major Cay, Exumas
highlights.snippet: Yes, the pigs are real, and yes, they will swim right up to your boat. You will need a day trip from Nassau via a charter flight to Staniel Cay (about $350–500 round trip per person) or a full-day …

highlights.title: Thunderball Grotto, Exumas
highlights.snippet: This underwater cave, made famous by the James Bond film, is a snorkeling paradise. Schools of tropical fish swirl through shafts of sunlight inside the grotto.

highlights.title: Pink Sands Beach, Harbour Island
highlights.snippet: A three-mile stretch of genuinely pink sand caused by crushed foraminifera shells. It is quieter and more exclusive than Nassau.

highlights.title: Fish Fry at Arawak Cay, Nassau
highlights.snippet: Skip the overpriced resort restaurants for at least one meal and head to Arawak Cay, a strip of local shacks serving conch fritters, cracked conch, and fresh grouper. A full meal runs $15–25.

destinations.name: Bali
destinations.season_note: Dry season Apr–Oct; rainy season Nov–Mar (mornings usually clear).

highlights.title: Uluwatu Temple at Sunset
highlights.snippet: Perched on a 70-metre cliff above the Indian Ocean, this 11th-century sea temple hosts a nightly Kecak fire dance as the sun drops. The setting is theatrically perfect.

highlights.title: Ubud Rice Terraces & Monkey Forest
highlights.snippet: Tegallalang's cascading rice terraces are Bali's most iconic landscape. Walk through in the early morning before the Instagram crowds arrive.

highlights.title: Mount Batur Sunrise Trek
highlights.snippet: A pre-dawn hike to the summit of an active volcano. You start at 3 AM and reach the crater rim by sunrise, where your guide cooks eggs in volcanic steam.

highlights.title: Seminyak Beach Clubs
highlights.snippet: Potato Head, Ku De Ta, and La Brisa define Bali's stylish daytime scene. Infinity pools, DJs, cocktails, and Balinese-fusion cuisine against an ocean backdrop.

highlights.title: Tirta Empul Water Temple, Tampaksiring
highlights.snippet: A holy spring temple where Balinese Hindus come for ritual purification. Visitors can participate — wear a sarong, follow the sequence of fountains, and immerse yourself in spring water that has be…

destinations.name: Banff
destinations.season_note: Two seasons: summer lakes (Jun–Sep) and ski season (Dec–Mar).

highlights.title: Lake Louise
highlights.snippet: The most photographed lake in Canada, and for good reason. The milky turquoise water is colored by glacial rock flour — the finer the summer sunlight, the more vivid the blue.

highlights.title: Moraine Lake
highlights.snippet: Many travelers say Moraine Lake is even more stunning than Lake Louise. The Valley of the Ten Peaks reflected in the impossibly blue water is the scene from the old Canadian $20 bill.

highlights.title: Icefields Parkway (Highway 93)
highlights.snippet: The 144-mile drive from Lake Louise to Jasper is routinely called the most scenic highway in the world. Glaciers, waterfalls, and wildlife at every turn.

highlights.title: Columbia Icefield Skywalk & Glacier Adventure
highlights.snippet: Step onto a glass-floored observation platform jutting 100 feet over the Sunwapta Valley, then ride a massive Ice Explorer bus onto the Athabasca Glacier itself. The combo ticket is C$120/adult.

highlights.title: Johnston Canyon
highlights.snippet: A 3.4-mile hike along a canyon trail with catwalks bolted to cliff faces above rushing water. The Lower Falls (1.1 km) is easy for all ages; the Upper Falls (2.7 km) is moderate.

destinations.name: Cabo
destinations.season_note: Whale season Dec–Apr; late summer is hot with storm risk.

highlights.title: El Arco de Cabo San Lucas
highlights.snippet: The iconic rock arch at the tip of the Baja Peninsula where the Pacific meets the Sea of Cortez. Take a glass-bottom boat or water taxi from Medano Beach for $15–20 per person.

highlights.title: Snorkeling at Chileno Bay
highlights.snippet: Cabo's best easily accessible snorkeling spot, with calm, clear water and abundant tropical fish. The bay is protected, so it's ideal even for beginners.

highlights.title: Whale Watching (December–April)
highlights.snippet: Humpback and grey whales migrate through the Sea of Cortez every winter, and Cabo is one of the best places on Earth to see them up close.

highlights.title: Sunset Dinner Cruise
highlights.snippet: Multiple operators run sunset cruises along the arch and coastline. The CaboRey catamaran offers an open bar and decent dinner for around $95–120 per person.

highlights.title: Medano Beach Day
highlights.snippet: Cabo's main swimmable beach is a scene unto itself. Rent a daybed at Mango Deck or The Office for $30–50 (redeemable on food and drinks). Jet ski rentals run $60–80 for 30 minutes.

destinations.name: Cancun
destinations.season_note: Dry season; avoid the Jun–Oct hurricane window where possible.

highlights.title: Chichén Itzá Day Trip
highlights.snippet: One of the New Seven Wonders of the World is a 2.5-hour drive from Cancún. The pyramid of Kukulkán is spectacular. Go with a guided tour that departs at 6 AM to arrive before the crowds and the heat.

highlights.title: Cenote Swimming
highlights.snippet: The Yucatán Peninsula has over 6,000 cenotes — natural limestone sinkholes filled with crystal-clear freshwater. Gran Cenote near Tulum and Cenote Ik Kil near Chichén Itzá are the most famous.

highlights.title: Isla Mujeres
highlights.snippet: A 15-minute ferry from Cancún's Hotel Zone takes you to this laid-back island. Rent a golf cart, drive to Punta Sur cliffs, and eat fresh ceviche at Playa Norte — consistently ranked among the worl…

highlights.title: Tulum Ruins
highlights.snippet: Mayan ruins perched on a cliff above the Caribbean Sea. The only major Mayan site on the coast. Arrive at 8 AM when gates open, then walk down to the beach below the ruins for a swim.

highlights.title: Underwater Museum (MUSA)
highlights.snippet: Over 500 life-size sculptures submerged in the Caribbean. Snorkel or scuba dive among the installations — it is art, marine conservation, and adventure in one.

destinations.name: Dominican Republic
destinations.season_note: Dry season Dec–Apr; whale season in Samaná is Jan–Mar.

highlights.title: Punta Cana Beach Day
highlights.snippet: Bávaro Beach and Playa Macao are the headliners, consistently ranked among the Caribbean's finest.

highlights.title: Zona Colonial, Santo Domingo
highlights.snippet: A day trip worth every minute of the 2.5-hour drive from Punta Cana. The oldest cathedral in the Americas (Catedral Primada de América, 1512), the Alcázar de Colón (Columbus's son's palace), and th…

highlights.title: Samaná Whale Watching (January–March)
highlights.snippet: Every winter, thousands of humpback whales migrate to the Bay of Samaná to breed and calve. This is one of the most reliable whale-watching experiences in the world.

highlights.title: Scape Park at Cap Cana
highlights.snippet: An adventure park about 15 minutes from most Punta Cana resorts featuring cenote-like freshwater lagoons (the Hoyo Azul is a stunning natural sinkhole), ziplines over the jungle, cultural experiences,.

highlights.title: Catamaran Snorkeling Tour
highlights.snippet: Multiple operators run half-day catamaran trips from Punta Cana to the natural pools of the Caribbean — shallow, calm areas where you can stand waist-deep in the ocean, drink rum punch, and snorkel am.

destinations.name: Dubai
destinations.season_note: Winter is peak — outdoor weather, festivals, highest prices.

highlights.title: Burj Khalifa, Downtown Dubai
highlights.snippet: Book the "At the Top" ticket for the 124th floor, or splurge on the 148th floor SKY lounge. Go at sunset for the best photos.

highlights.title: Old Dubai: Gold Souk & Spice Souk
highlights.snippet: Cross Dubai Creek on a traditional abra boat for one dirham and step into the oldest part of the city. The Gold Souk is the world's largest — prices are competitive and bargaining is expected.

highlights.title: Desert Safari
highlights.snippet: The quintessential Dubai experience. A 4x4 dune-bashing ride followed by a BBQ dinner under the stars with belly dancing, henna, and shisha.

highlights.title: Dubai Marina & JBR Walk
highlights.snippet: The Marina skyline at night is Dubai at its most photogenic. JBR (Jumeirah Beach Residence) has a public beach, waterfront dining, and Ain Dubai — the world's largest observation wheel.

highlights.title: Global Village
highlights.snippet: Open October through April, this massive outdoor theme park has pavilions from 90+ countries. The India Pavilion is always the loudest and most fun. Street food from every continent for under 20 AED.

destinations.name: Egypt
destinations.season_note: Cool season for the Nile valley; summers are fiercely hot.

highlights.title: Pyramids of Giza & the Sphinx
highlights.snippet: No amount of photos prepares you for the scale. The Great Pyramid stands 481 feet tall and was the tallest structure on earth for 3,800 years.

highlights.title: Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM)
highlights.snippet: The newly opened museum near Giza houses over 100,000 artifacts, including the complete Tutankhamun collection — all 5,000+ items from his tomb, most never before displayed.

highlights.title: Luxor — Valley of the Kings & Karnak Temple
highlights.snippet: Luxor is the world's greatest open-air museum. On the West Bank, the Valley of the Kings holds 63 royal tombs — your basic ticket (EGP 600/$12) includes entry to three tombs.

highlights.title: Nile River Cruise (Luxor to Aswan)
highlights.snippet: A 3–4 night cruise between Luxor and Aswan is the classic Egypt experience. The ship docks at temples along the way — Edfu (the best-preserved temple in Egypt), Kom Ombo (a double temple on a Nile …

highlights.title: Abu Simbel
highlights.snippet: Ramesses II's colossal temple, carved into a cliff face, with four 66-foot seated statues of the pharaoh guarding the entrance.

destinations.name: Fiji
destinations.season_note: Dry season May–Oct; cyclone season is Nov–Apr.

highlights.title: Nadi & the Sri Siva Subramaniya Temple
highlights.snippet: The largest Hindu temple in the Southern Hemisphere sits right in downtown Nadi, painted in vivid Dravidian colours. Free entry.

highlights.title: Yasawa Islands
highlights.snippet: A chain of volcanic islands with crystal water, dramatic cliffs, and almost no crowds. Take the Yasawa Flyer catamaran from Denarau ($130 round trip) to reach barefoot luxury resorts.

highlights.title: Coral Coast Snorkelling & Diving
highlights.snippet: Fiji is the soft coral capital of the world. The Great Astrolabe Reef near Kadavu is one of the largest barrier reefs on earth. Beginner-friendly dives start at $150 for two tanks.

highlights.title: Sigatoka Sand Dunes & Heritage Trail
highlights.snippet: Fiji's first national park, with archaeological sites dating back 2,600 years. The dunes themselves are hauntingly beautiful at sunset.

highlights.title: Suva — The Capital
highlights.snippet: Skip the resort bubble for a day and explore Suva. The Fiji Museum covers both indigenous Fijian and Indo-Fijian history, including the indenture period. The municipal market is enormous.

destinations.name: Florida
destinations.season_note: Dry, mild winter–spring; summer is hot, humid and hurricane-prone.

highlights.title: Walt Disney World, Orlando
highlights.snippet: The gold standard of family vacations. With four theme parks, two water parks, and Disney Springs, you need a minimum of four days to cover the highlights.

highlights.title: Kennedy Space Center, Cape Canaveral
highlights.snippet: An absolute must for families with curious kids. The Space Shuttle Atlantis exhibit is jaw-dropping, and the bus tour to Launch Complex 39 where Apollo missions launched gives you chills.

highlights.title: The Florida Keys & Key West
highlights.snippet: Drive the Overseas Highway from Miami to Key West, 113 miles of bridges and islands over turquoise water. It is one of America's most scenic drives.

highlights.title: Everglades Airboat Tour
highlights.snippet: An airboat ride through the River of Grass is unlike anything else in the US. You will see alligators, herons, and cypress swamps from just feet away.

highlights.title: Miami Beach & South Beach
highlights.snippet: Walk the Art Deco Historic District on Ocean Drive, swim at South Beach, and explore Wynwood Walls for street art. For Indian families, head to Deccan Spice or Ghee Indian Kitchen in Miami proper.

destinations.name: France
destinations.season_note: Late spring and early autumn beat the August crowds and closures.

highlights.title: Eiffel Tower & Seine River Cruise
highlights.snippet: The Eiffel Tower at night, when it sparkles on the hour, is genuinely magical. Skip the summit queue — the second floor view is nearly identical.

highlights.title: Louvre Museum
highlights.snippet: The world's largest and most visited museum. Do not try to see everything — focus on the Mona Lisa wing (Italian Renaissance), Winged Victory, and the Egyptian antiquities. Budget 3–4 hours minimum.

highlights.title: Provence: Lavender Fields & Villages
highlights.snippet: Visit in late June through mid-July when the lavender is in peak bloom. The Luberon villages — Gordes, Roussillon, Bonnieux — are achingly beautiful.

highlights.title: Mont Saint-Michel
highlights.snippet: A medieval abbey on a tidal island in Normandy. It looks like a fantasy painting and is one of France's most visited landmarks. Go at high tide when the island is completely surrounded by water.

highlights.title: French Riviera: Nice, Monaco & Cannes
highlights.snippet: The Promenade des Anglais in Nice, the Casino de Monte-Carlo in Monaco, and the Croisette in Cannes — the Côte d'Azur is European glamour distilled.

destinations.name: Goa
destinations.season_note: Dry, sunny winter season; monsoon (Jun–Sep) shuts most beach shacks.

highlights.title: Old Goa Churches
highlights.snippet: The Basilica of Bom Jesus, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, holds the remains of St. Francis Xavier. Se Cathedral next door is the largest church in Asia.

highlights.title: Palolem Beach, South Goa
highlights.snippet: A crescent of sand lined with colourful beach huts and coconut palms. South Goa is quieter, cleaner, and more family-friendly than the north.

highlights.title: Fontainhas Latin Quarter, Panaji
highlights.snippet: Narrow streets lined with pastel-painted Portuguese houses, art galleries, and bakeries selling bebinca. Walking through Fontainhas feels like Lisbon transplanted to the tropics.

highlights.title: Dudhsagar Falls
highlights.snippet: A four-tiered waterfall plunging 310 metres through lush jungle on the Goa-Karnataka border. Best visited during monsoon (July–September) when the falls are at full force.

highlights.title: Saturday Night Market, Arpora
highlights.snippet: A sprawling bazaar with live music, international food stalls, handicraft vendors, and a party atmosphere. It runs only on Saturdays from November to April.

destinations.name: Greece
destinations.season_note: Islands are best late May–early Oct; July–August is peak-price.

highlights.title: Santorini Sunset at Oia
highlights.snippet: Position yourself at the castle ruins in Oia by 6 PM. The sunset here is objectively one of the best in the world. Stay in a cave hotel in Fira or Oia for the full caldera view.

highlights.title: Athens: Acropolis & Parthenon
highlights.snippet: The Acropolis is to Greece what the Taj Mahal is to India — the one thing you cannot skip. Visit at opening (8 AM) or late afternoon to avoid midday heat.

highlights.title: Mykonos: Beaches & Little Venice
highlights.snippet: The party island of Greece, but also genuinely beautiful. Little Venice's waterfront bars at sunset, the iconic windmills, and Paradise Beach are the highlights.

highlights.title: Meteora Monasteries
highlights.snippet: Six Byzantine monasteries perched on towering rock pillars in central Greece. Less visited than the islands but equally jaw-dropping. A day trip from Kalabaka — hire a driver or join a sunrise tour.

highlights.title: Crete: Samaria Gorge & Elafonisi Beach
highlights.snippet: Greece's largest island has its own mountain range, its own cuisine, and Europe's longest gorge hike (16 km).

destinations.name: Hawaii
destinations.season_note: Great most of the year; whale season Dec–Apr, surf peaks in winter.

highlights.title: Nā Pali Coast, Kauai
highlights.snippet: By boat, helicopter, or the Kalalau Trail, the Nā Pali Coast is Hawaii's most dramatic scenery. Towering emerald cliffs plunging into sapphire ocean.

highlights.title: Haleakalā Sunrise, Maui
highlights.snippet: Watch the sunrise from 10,023 feet above the clouds inside a dormant volcanic crater. Reserve a spot in advance (required by the National Park Service).

highlights.title: Waikiki Beach & Diamond Head, Oahu
highlights.snippet: The most famous beach in the Pacific. Waikiki is perfect for families — gentle waves, warm water, and surfing lessons everywhere.

highlights.title: Volcanoes National Park, Big Island
highlights.snippet: Walk across a live volcanic landscape. The Kīlauea caldera, steam vents, and lava tubes are otherworldly.

highlights.title: Snorkelling at Molokini Crater, Maui
highlights.snippet: A partially submerged volcanic crater forms a natural crescent that shelters some of the clearest water in Hawaii. Visibility can reach 150 feet.

destinations.name: Himachal Pradesh
destinations.season_note: Spring and autumn are clearest; avoid Jul–Aug monsoon landslides.

highlights.title: Rohtang Pass & Atal Tunnel
highlights.snippet: The 10-km Atal Tunnel (opened 2020) connects Manali to Lahaul-Spiti, making what was once a dangerous seasonal road into a year-round route.

highlights.title: Old Manali & Solang Valley
highlights.snippet: Old Manali has evolved from a backpacker village into a vibrant café and culture scene. Solang Valley offers paragliding, zorbing, and skiing in winter. The Beas River runs through everything.

highlights.title: McLeod Ganj & Tsuglagkhang Complex
highlights.snippet: Visit the Dalai Lama's residence and the Tibetan museum. The Bhagsu Waterfall trail is an easy 45-minute walk.

highlights.title: Shimla Ridge & Mall Road
highlights.snippet: The former summer capital of British India still carries that colonial charm. Walk the Ridge at sunset, visit Christ Church, and take the heritage toy train from Kalka to Shimla — a UNESCO World He…

highlights.title: Kasol & Kheerganga Trek
highlights.snippet: The Parvati Valley draws both adventure seekers and those looking for solitude. Kasol is the base camp. The Kheerganga trek (12 km one way) ends at natural hot springs at 3,050 metres.

destinations.name: Iceland
destinations.season_note: Summer for the full ring road; Sep–Oct and Feb–Mar for auroras with daylight.

highlights.title: The Golden Circle
highlights.snippet: This 300-kilometre loop from Reykjavik covers the three essentials: Thingvellir National Park (where the Eurasian and North American plates meet), the Geysir geothermal area (where Strokkur erupts eve.

highlights.title: Blue Lagoon
highlights.snippet: The milky-blue geothermal pool set in a black lava field is Iceland's most famous image. The Comfort package starts at $75 (includes entry, silica mud mask, and one drink).

highlights.title: South Coast Waterfalls & Black Sand Beach
highlights.snippet: Drive the Ring Road south from Reykjavik to hit Seljalandsfoss (walk behind it), Skógafoss (climb the 527 steps beside it), and Reynisfjara black sand beach with its hexagonal basalt columns.

highlights.title: Glacier Hiking on Sólheimajökull
highlights.snippet: Walk on an actual glacier tongue with crampons and an ice axe. Guided tours run about $85–100 for 3 hours. No experience needed, but you must be reasonably fit.

highlights.title: Northern Lights (September–March)
highlights.snippet: Reykjavik's light pollution is manageable but driving 30 minutes outside the city dramatically improves visibility. Guided tours run $60–80 and include hot chocolate and blankets.

destinations.name: Italy
destinations.season_note: Shoulder months have the weather without the peak crowds.

highlights.title: Rome: Colosseum, Vatican & Trastevere
highlights.snippet: The Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill are a single ticket. Book skip-the-line at the Vatican — the Sistine Chapel is overwhelming in person.

highlights.title: Florence: Uffizi & Duomo

highlights.title: Gardens by the Bay & Supertree Grove
highlights.snippet: The Supertree light show at 7:45 PM and 8:45 PM is free and spectacular. The Cloud Forest dome and Flower Dome are worth the entry fee. Budget two hours minimum.

highlights.title: Marina Bay Sands & Merlion Park
highlights.snippet: The rooftop infinity pool is hotel-guests-only, but the SkyPark observation deck is open to all. Walk along the Helix Bridge to Merlion Park for the classic Singapore photo.

highlights.title: Hawker Centers
highlights.snippet: Singapore's hawker centres are UNESCO-recognised. Maxwell Food Centre (near Chinatown) for Hainanese chicken rice, Lau Pa Sat for satay street at night, and Tekka Centre in Little India for the bes…

highlights.title: Sentosa Island
highlights.snippet: Universal Studios, Adventure Cove Waterpark, the S.E.A. Aquarium, and Siloso Beach packed into one island. Perfect for families with kids. Take the free Sentosa Express monorail from VivoCity mall.

highlights.title: Little India & Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple
highlights.snippet: Walk through the colourful streets of Serangoon Road. Visit the temple, eat at Komala Vilas or Banana Leaf Apolo (legendary fish head curry), and stock up on spices, sarees, and gold at Mustafa Cen…

destinations.name: South Africa
destinations.season_note: Dry-season safari May–Sep; Cape Town is best Nov–Mar (see guide).

highlights.title: Kruger National Park (Self-Drive Safari)
highlights.snippet: Unlike East African parks where you must hire an expensive guide, Kruger lets you drive your own rental car through the bush.

highlights.title: Table Mountain, Cape Town
highlights.snippet: Take the rotating cable car to the 1,085-meter summit for panoramic views of Cape Town, Robben Island, and the Atlantic. Tickets are R440 ($24) return — book online to skip the queue.

highlights.title: Robben Island
highlights.snippet: The prison where Nelson Mandela spent 18 of his 27 years of imprisonment. Tours are led by former political prisoners, making this one of the most powerful museum experiences in the world.

highlights.title: Cape Winelands — Stellenbosch & Franschhoek
highlights.snippet: World-class wine estates just 45 minutes from Cape Town. Stellenbosch has over 200 wineries; Franschhoek is the culinary capital. Wine tastings run R80–150 ($5–8) for 5–6 wines.

highlights.title: The Garden Route
highlights.snippet: Drive from Cape Town to Port Elizabeth along one of the world's great coastal roads.

destinations.name: Spain
destinations.season_note: Spring and autumn; August is hot and crowded on the coasts.

highlights.title: Sagrada Familia, Barcelona
highlights.snippet: Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece has been under construction since 1882 and is targeted for completion around 2026.

highlights.title: The Alhambra, Granada
highlights.snippet: A Moorish palace complex that rivals the Taj Mahal for sheer architectural beauty.

highlights.title: Prado Museum, Madrid
highlights.snippet: One of the world's greatest art museums, housing Velázquez's Las Meninas, Goya's Black Paintings, and Bosch's Garden of Earthly Delights.

highlights.title: La Rambla & Gothic Quarter, Barcelona
highlights.snippet: Barcelona's most famous boulevard runs from Plaça de Catalunya to the waterfront. The adjoining Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) is a labyrinth of medieval streets, hidden plazas, and tiny tapas bars.

highlights.title: Flamenco in Seville
highlights.snippet: An authentic tablao (flamenco venue) in Seville is visceral in a way that no video can capture.

destinations.name: Sri Lanka
destinations.season_note: West/south coasts and hill country are at their best Dec–Mar.

highlights.title: Sigiriya Rock Fortress
highlights.snippet: A fifth-century palace built atop a 200-metre volcanic plug, surrounded by landscaped gardens and frescoed caves. The climb is steep but manageable.

highlights.title: Train from Kandy to Ella
highlights.snippet: Routinely listed among the world's most scenic rail journeys. Seven hours through tea plantations, waterfalls, and cloud forest.

highlights.title: Galle Fort
highlights.snippet: A walled Dutch colonial fort on the southwest coast, now filled with boutique hotels, cafés, and galleries. Walk the ramparts at sunset.

highlights.title: Yala National Park Safari
highlights.snippet: The highest density of leopards anywhere on earth. Morning jeep safaris offer excellent chances of sighting. Yala also has elephants, sloth bears, and crocodiles.

highlights.title: Jaffna & the North
highlights.snippet: Still undervisited since the civil war ended in 2009, Jaffna offers Tamil Hindu culture, Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil, and extraordinary seafood — the Jaffna crab curry is legendary.

destinations.name: Switzerland
destinations.season_note: Summer hiking (Jun–Sep) and ski season (Dec–Mar).

highlights.title: Jungfraujoch, Top of Europe
highlights.snippet: A cogwheel railway climbs to 3,454 metres through the Eiger's interior. The observation deck offers views across the Aletsch Glacier. Yes, the "Bollywood platform" with Hindi signs is real.

highlights.title: Lake Lucerne Boat Cruise
highlights.snippet: A paddle steamer across Switzerland's most beautiful lake, ringed by mountains. Combine it with the Mount Pilatus golden round trip — boat, cogwheel train, cable car, and panorama gondola in a loop.

highlights.title: Interlaken Adventure Sports
highlights.snippet: The adventure capital of Europe. Paragliding over the lake with Alpine peaks behind you is a life-changing 15 minutes. Also available: canyoning, skydiving, bungee jumping, and river rafting.

highlights.title: Zermatt & the Matterhorn
highlights.snippet: The iconic pyramid-shaped peak is Switzerland's calling card. Zermatt is car-free and postcard-perfect.

highlights.title: Grindelwald First Cliff Walk
highlights.snippet: A metal walkway bolted into a cliff face 2,000 metres above the valley floor. The First Flyer zip line (800 metres long) and the First Glider (eagle-eye chairlift) add adrenaline.

destinations.name: Tamil Nadu
destinations.season_note: Coolest months; Pongal in mid-January. Coastal rain peaks Oct–Dec.

highlights.title: Meenakshi Amman Temple, Madurai
highlights.snippet: This is not just a temple; it is a small city. The four towering gopurams (gateway towers) covered in thousands of brightly painted stucco figures are the defining image of Tamil Nadu.

highlights.title: Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram) Shore Temples
highlights.snippet: A UNESCO World Heritage Site where 7th-century Pallava rock-cut temples meet the Bay of Bengal.

highlights.title: Brihadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur
highlights.snippet: Built by Raja Raja Chola I over a thousand years ago, this UNESCO temple's 216-foot vimana (tower) was the tallest structure in India when completed.

highlights.title: Pondicherry (Puducherry)
highlights.snippet: A former French colony that still feels convincingly Mediterranean on certain streets.

highlights.title: Rameswaram & Pamban Bridge
highlights.snippet: One of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites and the closest point in India to Sri Lanka.

destinations.name: Thailand
destinations.season_note: Cool, dry season; Songkran in mid-April.

highlights.title: Grand Palace & Wat Pho, Bangkok
highlights.snippet: The Grand Palace complex is Thailand's equivalent of the Taj Mahal — non-negotiable. Arrive at 8:30 AM when the gates open to beat tour groups.

highlights.title: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar & Temples
highlights.snippet: The old city has over 300 temples within its moated walls. Doi Suthep at sunset is magnificent.

highlights.title: Phi Phi Islands Day Trip
highlights.snippet: Take the speedboat from Phuket or Krabi. Maya Bay is open again after its environmental recovery. Snorkelling here rivals anything in Southeast Asia. Go early to avoid the midday crowds.

highlights.title: Floating Markets, Bangkok
highlights.snippet: Damnoen Saduak is the famous one, but Amphawa (open weekends) is more authentic and less touristy. Go in the morning, eat pad thai from a boat, and take the firefly tour at dusk.

highlights.title: Elephant Nature Park, Chiang Mai
highlights.snippet: Skip the riding camps. This ethical sanctuary lets you feed, bathe, and walk with rescued elephants. Book the full-day experience at least two weeks in advance — it sells out.

destinations.name: Uttarakhand
destinations.season_note: Char Dham season May–Jun and Sep–Oct; winters are bitter at altitude.

highlights.title: Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat, Rishikesh
highlights.snippet: Every evening at sunset, priests perform an elaborate fire ceremony on the banks of the Ganges. The chanting, the bells, the floating diyas on the water — it is one of India's most moving rituals.

highlights.title: Whitewater Rafting on the Ganges
highlights.snippet: Rishikesh is India's rafting capital, with rapids ranging from Grade I to Grade IV between Shivpuri and the Lakshman Jhula stretch.

highlights.title: Jim Corbett National Park
highlights.snippet: India's oldest national park and one of the best places to spot a Bengal tiger in the wild.

highlights.title: Char Dham Yatra
highlights.snippet: The full circuit — Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, Badrinath — takes 10–12 days and is one of Hinduism's most sacred pilgrimages.

highlights.title: Mussoorie & Landour
highlights.snippet: The Queen of the Hills retains its Raj-era charm, especially in Landour, the quieter cantonment area above Mussoorie where Ruskin Bond still lives.

destinations.name: Vietnam
destinations.season_note: Drier months overall — the country spans three climate zones.

highlights.title: Ha Long Bay Overnight Cruise
highlights.snippet: Take a two-day, one-night junk boat cruise through 1,600 limestone karsts rising from emerald water. Kayak through sea caves, swim at hidden beaches, and wake up to mist-covered islands.

highlights.title: Hoi An Ancient Town
highlights.snippet: A UNESCO World Heritage Site with Japanese bridges, Chinese temples, and French colonial architecture. Get clothes custom-tailored in 24 hours — Hoi An is famous for it.

highlights.title: Hanoi Old Quarter & Street Food
highlights.snippet: The 36 streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter are organised by trade — silk street, silver street, paper street.

highlights.title: Ho Chi Minh City: War Remnants Museum & Cu Chi Tunnels
highlights.snippet: Regardless of your politics, these are profoundly moving. The War Remnants Museum should be a mandatory stop.

highlights.title: Ninh Binh: Tam Coc Boat Ride
highlights.snippet: Called "Ha Long Bay on land," the Tam Coc boat ride through rice paddies and limestone caves is ethereally beautiful. Less touristy than Ha Long and just 90 minutes from Hanoi.
